correctness.rationale: For N=d+1 real finite-metric points with sole distance 0<t<=1 shortened, the primal transport norm is m-(1-t)min(|x0|,|x1|) exactly when x0 and x1 have opposite signs; otherwise m. A positive-negative sign chamber has equilateral volume binomial(d-1,p-1)/d!, and the short-edge opposite-sign chambers universally expand by 1/t, proved using U=min(A,B) with survival (1-u)^(d-1) and exact integral. Vandermonde yields vol P=binom(2d,d)/d! [d+(d-1)t]/[(2d-1)t]. In polar Q1, ordering of N potential values gives (d+1)! unit-gap simplices; the distinguished difference has beta-mixture density 2[d-(d-1)u]/(d+1). Restricting |f0-f1|<=t yields vol Q=t[2d-(d-1)t]. Differentiate product: M_d proportional to [d+(d-1)t][2d-(d-1)t], unique maximum t=d/[2(d-1)] for d>=3, exact gain and 1/8 asymptotic. Independently checked both closed profiles using exact rational identities d=2..15 and SciPy geometric primal/polar computations d=2,3,4 at t=1/2,3/4,1; finite hull topology does not replace analytic proof.
residual_risks: Coordinate volumes are ordinary molecule-coordinate Lebesgue volumes, not Euclidean volume in the original zero-mass subspace; product is affine invariant.
Finite primal/polar hull triangulations use floating-point combinatorial facet selection, with exact rational determinants; analytic proof handles all dimensions and real t.
